newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Islamist MPs call off parliament boycott.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Islamist MPs call off parliament boycott.

text.p: Jordan's Islamists said on Sunday they decided to end a parliamentary boycott after the pro-government dominated chamber agreed to a special session to debate Israel's settlement policy in Palestinian areas.

Jordan's 15 Islamist deputies and their leftist allies briefly disrupted parliament on Wednesday and announced a boycott of future sessions in protest at what they said was a weak government reaction to Israel's settlement policy in Arab East Jerusalem.

"There is no longer any justification to continue the boycott after a majority of deputies voted in favour of our statement asking for special session to discuss Jewish settlement in Palestinian areas," leading Islamist deputy Abdullah Akaylah told Reuters.

The vote in the 80-seat chamber was 36-30 in favour of the Islamist's proposal to hold a special session on Tuesday to debate an Israeli settlement drive in the West Bank, which has outraged many Jordanians with family ties to Palestinians.

The Islamist-led opposition are demanding a tougher government reaction against Israeli plans to build 6,500 new homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem and also want a severing in diplomatic ties established after a 1994 peace treaty.

The Islamists' decision comes only three days after King Hussein criticised them for walking out of parliament, saying that "deputies were not elected just to withdraw from parliament every now and then", he said.

"What His Majesty King Hussein uttered is a matter of appreciation and respect and we realise that withdrawing from parliament does not solve a problem...but it was an expression of protest," Akaylah said.
